claims.text: In-situ reactive processing can form TiC and Al2O3 reinforcements within an NbMoCrTiAl high-entropy-alloy matrix.
The resulting ceramic reinforcements will be fine and uniformly dispersed.
The initial as-cast NbMoCrTiAl alloy is single-phase and has a homogeneous matrix microstructure.
Powder-metallurgy processing is a viable route for in-situ formation of the ceramic-reinforced NbMoCrTiAl composite.
The target composite contains approximately 7 vol.% Al2O3 and about 30 vol.% TiC.
The mechanical benefits should occur at ambient temperature.
The mechanical benefits should persist at moderately elevated temperatures.
Maintaining a nanoscale dispersion and strong particle-matrix interfacial bonding is required for the benefits.
Particle agglomeration, coarse phases, coarsening, or interfacial degradation will suppress the proposed improvements.
Fine ceramic reinforcements act as load-transfer agents in the metallic matrix.
Fine ceramic reinforcements act as crack deflectors in the metallic matrix.
The ceramic particles induce strain hardening.
Crack deflection or blunting by the ceramic particles enhances fracture resistance.
The composite microstructure mitigates localized deformation and thereby improves ductility.
Mitigation of localized deformation increases Young's modulus.
The reinforced composite will exhibit at least a 50% increase in fracture strength relative to as-cast NbMoCrTiAl.
The reinforced composite will have improved ductility relative to the as-cast alloy.
The reinforced composite will have a higher Young's modulus relative to the as-cast alloy.
The reinforced composite will have improved fracture toughness relative to the as-cast alloy.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the hypothesis applies only when a fine, uniform ceramic dispersion and strong interfaces are successfully produced, but the falsification rule treats failure to produce that microstructure as falsification. This confounds failure to implement the intervention with failure of the hypothesized mechanism under its stated applicability conditions.
